Yes, tags are per kinetic group today. A mixed group is one group holding a plain binding and a chemistry step that take up the same metabolite, for example a dead-end E(Q) + B → E(B, Q) grouped with a fused E(A) + B → E(P, Q). The enumerator builds such groups because the two steps share their constants.

Under the affinity reading of B1, the binding needs K_I → ∞ while the chemistry step only needs blocking. Kept tied, the chemistry step is dragged along, which can contradict Haldane: 90 of 105 expand_bibi failures and all 39 allo_bibi failures. Untied in the inactive state (still tied in the active state), every allo_bibi mechanism is well defined.

So this card depends on B1:
- affinity for bindings: untie in the inactive state, or forbid mixed :OnlyA groups (the enumerator then never tags such a group :OnlyA);
- kinetic block for every step: no conflict, the group stays tied.

Forbidding is the simplest to explain. The vertical slice can count how many enumerated mechanisms would lose an :OnlyA tag.

Follow-up: either flag, and enumeration builds the RE one. A group carries one RE/SS flag, and the enumerator builds this exact group both ways: init_bibi/57 has (E(A) + B <--> E(P, Q), E(Q) + B <--> E(B, Q)), and init_bibi/56 has (E(A) + B ⇌ E(P, Q), E(Q) + B ⇌ E(B, Q)). When it builds seeds, the enumerator flips groups to SS until no chemistry sits in rapid equilibrium with both the substrate and the product side. An RE fused binding survives that when the releases from its merged complex are SS; an RE Theorell–Chance step never does. RE fused bindings occur in 76 of 239 bi-bi seeds and 90 of 264 ping-pong-capable ones.

The groups come from merging. The seed group says B binds E(A) and E(Q) with one Kd. Merging E(A, B) into E(P, Q) keeps the group, so the dead-end Kd of B at E(Q) is tied to the constant of B binding into the merged complex. The developer docs allow a fused and a plain binding of one metabolite to share a group, so this is by design.

Corrections to my earlier reply:

- The chemistry member is always a fused binding, never Theorell–Chance (858 mixed groups checked).
- The plain member is not always a dead end: init_bibi/170 has catalytic plain members.
- Every allosteric mixed group is :OnlyA, because the expander tags every group that holds chemistry: 71 in allo_bibi (all SS) and 172 in expand_bibi (45 RE, 127 SS).

How this plays with B1:

- Bindings by affinity, each member in its own class: the plain member is an affinity door, so its dead-end form empties, and the fused member is blocked. Every enumerated mechanism with a mixed group then equals deletion, apart from one ping-pong that fails for its island anyway. No enumeration change.
- Kinetic block for steady-state bindings: the tied dead-end form hangs at equilibrium through the chemistry's ratio. That is where the enumerated phantoms come from: allo_bibi/1447 is 0.4% from deletion and allo_terbi/156 19%. You would then need to forbid mixed :OnlyA groups, or give a merged binding its own group at the merge; both change enumeration.

I added the second of those as an option.
